chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'A man buys a slave and his property.' He said, 'There is no objection to that.' I asked, 'And the slave's property may be more than what he was bought for?' He said, 'There is no objection.'

key_terms.اشْتَرَاهُ بِهِ: What he was bought for / The purchase price
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكَ: The slave (male), referring to the person purchased
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does buying a slave include acquiring their personal property, even if it is worth more than the slave's price?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *mal al-mamluk* (property owned by the slave), establishing that the master acquires the slave's assets regardless of their value relative to the purchase price. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the slave's property is not automatically forfeited or capped, emphasizing the master's full ownership rights over both the person and their existing wealth.
